1	# Epic 1 Context: Foundation & Session Management
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	This epic delivers the scaffold every other feature depends on: the pinned-stack project setup with its core infrastructure verified working together, the full visual design-token system, email/password authentication with silent session refresh, the session-expiry recovery overlay, and a base navigation shell with placeholders for everything not yet built. It is delivered first because every later epic assumes this foundation — DI, networking, error handling, session state, design tokens, and navigation — already exists and is stable. Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
17	
18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
60	- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).
61

23	
24	# Architecture Spine — Cerne
25	
26	## Design Paradigm
27	
28	**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**
29	
30	- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
31	- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
32	- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
33	- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.
34	
35	```mermaid
36	flowchart TD
37	    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
38	        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
39	        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
40	        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
41	        P --> D
42	        DA --> D
43	    end
44	    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, VaultStatus, design_tokens)"]
45	    D --> Core
46	    DA --> Core
47	    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
48	    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
49	```
50	
51	## Invariants & Rules
52	
53	### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)
54	
55	- **Binds:** all features
56	- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
57	- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.
58	
59	### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)
60	
61	- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
62	- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
63	- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.
64	
65	### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`
66	
67	- **Binds:** all
68	- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
69	- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature. `AuthInvalid` can only ever originate from `POST /auth/login` — no biometric/PIN check ever reaches the server (AD-14), so no feature maps a local vault failure to this code.
70	
71	### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`
72	
73	- **Binds:** the API client
74	- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
75	- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.
76	
77	### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy
78	
79	- **Binds:** every network call
80	- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
81	- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
82	
83	### AD-6 — `entries` owns `Entry` from RF01 onward; every other feature reaches it only through a domain-layer port
84	
85	- **Binds:** RF01 (capture → entries, the *first* consumer — delivery order builds RF01 three units before RF06/RF07), RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
86	- **Prevents:** (a) RF01 inventing its own local `Entry` model/repository/cache box because `features/entries/` "doesn't exist yet" at its position in the delivery order, which RF06/RF07 would then duplicate; (b) any feature reaching into `entries`'s `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
87	- **Rule:** `features/entries/` is scaffolded at RF01 (not RF06/RF07) because RF01 is the first unit that must call `POST /entries` (requirements.md §6.2). From RF01 on, `entries/domain` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create`, `read` — see AD-11), and the entries Hive box. `entries` exposes an abstract `CreateEntryUseCase`/`SaveEntryUseCase`-shaped port; RF01's `capture` feature and RF10's `chat` feature are both *consumers* — each only ever imports and injects that abstract type from `entries/domain`, never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`. RF06/RF07 extend the same `EntriesRepository` port with `list`/`search` methods; they do not introduce a second entry model or a second owner. The port's `create` is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`: a second call for a `chatMessageId` that already has an entry never creates a duplicate — the implementation (not the port's type signature) is responsible for this check, binding on RF10's build.
88	
89	### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references
90	
91	- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
92	- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
93	- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.
94	
95	### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth
96	
97	- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
98	- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
99	- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream. `SessionStatus` governs *server session validity only* — it composes with the local vault gate per AD-14, it does not replace it.
100	
101	### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
102	
103	- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
104	- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
105	- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Plain reads (`GET /entries`, `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET .../messages`) transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. **Semantic search is the one read exception:** `GET /entries/search` has no client-side vector index to fall back to, so with no connectivity it also resolves to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)`, same as a write — it is never served from cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
106	
107	### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)
108	
109	- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
110	- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
111	- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from three inputs: `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and the transient per-entry write state (AD-9) — which is itself one of three values: no pending write (→ `Synchronized`), a write in flight (→ `Synchronizing`), or the in-flight write's `Future` resolved to `Left(Failure)` (→ `Synchronization error`, held until the next write attempt reconciles it). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
112	
113	### AD-11 — Entry immutability
114	
115	- **Binds:** the entries feature
116	- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
117	- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.
118	
119	### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`
120	
121	- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02, RF04, or RF07
122	- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
123	- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`), RF07's composite auth × sync × data state, and RF04's chat message stream (append-only, streaming/SSE, not a single fetch) each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`. RF08's proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto RF04's existing chat state, not a parallel `Resource<T>`.
124	
125	### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`
126	
127	- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
128	- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
129	- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. The helper's own `Future` always completes independently of the caller: RF10 may `await` it before updating its button state, and RF08 must be able to call it **without** awaiting (fire-and-forget) so a slow/failed insight generation never blocks or delays the chat stream. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.
130	
131	### AD-14 — One `go_router` redirect composes exactly two gates, in a fixed order: vault, then session
132	
133	- **Binds:** F000 (builds the redirect skeleton + `SessionStatus` half), RF03 (plugs the vault half into the same redirect)
134	- **Prevents:** F000 and RF03 each building an independent navigation gate (two competing `redirect` callbacks, or RF03 bolting a second check onto screens individually) — `go_router` supports only one top-level `redirect`, so two independently-built gates cannot both "just work."
135	- **Rule:** the redirect composes exactly two domain-level streams, evaluated in this order: (1) `VaultStatus` (local-only — biometric/PIN unlocked, Face-ID-failed-offer-PIN, or locked after the 5-minute background timeout; RF03 exposes it from `features/vault/domain` the same way auth exposes `SessionStatus`, AD-8) — checked *first*, before any network state, because it gates whether the app may show anything at all; then (2) `SessionStatus` (AD-8) once the vault is unlocked. Neither gate ever reaches the server to validate itself (`POST /auth/login` is the only path that can produce `AuthInvalid`, per AD-3) — the vault is validated entirely on-device, consistent with the backend having no biometric-unlock endpoint.
136	
137	### AD-15 — The local cache is a projection, never a query engine
138	
139	- **Binds:** `entries`, `chat` — every feature with a `hive_ce` box `[ADOPTED, promoted from the F000 forge session]`
140	- **Prevents:** a unit adding local filtering, joining, or sorting logic "for performance" or "for offline support," which would then disagree with the server's own filter semantics (AD-9's offline read rule assumes the cache's content is a verbatim copy, not a re-derived view).
141	- **Rule:** every query dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`/`dateTo`, semantic search, pagination cursor) is a server-side query parameter per `openapi.yaml`. A `hive_ce` box stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id (or by session id for messages); no feature ever filters, joins, sorts, or re-derives a different view from a cached collection — a cache miss or a dimension not covered by AD-9's offline-read rule surfaces `Failure.networkOffline`, it is never approximated locally.
142	
143	## Consistency Conventions
144	
145	| Concern | Convention |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
148	| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
149	| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
150	| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
151	| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
152	| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
153	| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |

3	The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

7	| File | What it is |
8	|---|---|

10	| `error-taxonomy.md` | The 13 error codes, with HTTP status and `retryable` |

1	# Error taxonomy — 13 codes
2	
3	Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.
4	
5	| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
8	| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
9	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
10	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
11	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
12	| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
13	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
14	| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
15	| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
16	| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
17	| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
18	| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
19	| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |
20	
21	**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
22	- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
23	- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.
24	
25	**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

You have to: - Define a constructor + properties - Override `toString`, `operator ==`, `hashCode` - Implement a `copyWith` method to clone the object - Handle (de)serialization Implementing all of this can take hundreds of lines, which are error-prone and affect the readability of your model significantly. [Third-party tools](#third-party-tools) - [DartJ](#dartj) - [Sponsors](#sponsors) # How to use ## Install To use [Freezed], you will need your typical [build_runner]/code-generator setup.\ First, install [build_runner] and [Freezed] by adding them to your `pubspec.yaml` file: For a Flutter project: ```console flutter pub add \ dev:build_runner \ freezed_annotation \ dev:freezed # if using freezed to generate fromJson/toJson, also add: flutter pub add json_annotation dev:json_serializable ``` For a Dart project: ```console dart pub add \ dev:build_runner \ freezed_annotation \ dev:freezed # if using freezed to generate fromJson/toJson, also add: dart pub add json_annotation dev:json_serializable ``` This installs three packages: - [build_runner](https://pub.dev/packages/build_runner), the tool to run code-generators - [freezed], the code generator - [freezed_annotation](https://pub.dev/packages/freezed_annotation), a package containing annotations for [freezed]. ### Disabling invalid_annotation_target warning and warning in generates files If you plan on using [Freezed] in combination with `json_serializable`, recent versions of `json_serializable` and `meta` may require you to disable the `invalid_annotation_target` warning. To do that, you can add the following to the `analysis_options.yaml` file at the root of your project: ```yaml analyzer: errors: invalid_annotation_target: ignore ``` ## Run the generator To run the code generator, execute the following command: ``` dart run build_runner watch -d ``` Note that like most code-generators, [Freezed] will need you to both import the annotation ([freezed_annotation]) and use the `part` keyword on the top of your files. As such, a file that wants to use [Freezed] will start with: ```dart import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart'; part 'my_file.freezed.dart'; ``` **CONSIDER** also importing `package:flutter/foundation.dart`.\ The reason being, importing `foundation.dart` also imports classes to make an object nicely readable in Flutter's devtool.\ If you import `foundation.dart`, [Freezed] will automatically do it for you. ## Creating a Model using Freezed Freezed offers two ways of creating data-classes: - [Primary constructors](#primary-constructors) ; where you define a constructor and Freezed generates the associated fields. This is simulating the [Primary Constructor](https://github.com/dart-lang/language/issues/2364) using `factory`. - [Classic classes](#classic-classes), where you write a normal Dart class and Freezed only handles `toString/==/copyWith` ### Primary constructors **Note** As of Dart 3.13, primary constructors are a stable feature of Dart. This means that you no longer need to use `freezed` to generate primary constructors. But you can stick to using Freezed for ==/toString/etc: ```dart import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart'; part 'main.freezed.dart'; part 'main.g.dart'; @freezed class Person({ required final String firstName, required final String lastName, required final int age, required final DateTime birthDate, }) with _$Person; void main() { var person = Person( firstName: 'John', lastName: 'Doe', age: 42, birthDate: DateTime(1978), ); person = person.copyWith(age: 43); } ``` --- Freezed implements Primary Constructors by relying on `factory` constructors. The idea is, you define a `factory` and Freezed generates everything else: ```dart import 'package:freezed_annotation/freezed_annotation.dart'; // required: associates our `main.dart` with the code generated by Freezed part 'main.freezed.dart'; // optional: Since our Person class is serializable, we must add this line. // But if Person was not serializable, we could skip it. part 'main.g.dart'; @freezed abstract class Person with _$Person { const factory Person({ required String firstName, required String lastName, required int age, }) = _Person; factory Person.fromJson(Map json) => _$PersonFromJson(json); } ```

4	## Cerne
5	
6	Reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. Flutter/Dart (pinned via fvm), `flutter_bloc`, Clean Architecture. Product spec, screen flow and delivery order: `docs/input/requirements.md`. Visual reference: `docs/input/prototype/`. Backend contract (already built, frozen): `docs/input/backend/`.
7	
8	## Policy
9	
10	- Where `docs/input/` is silent on a technical choice, decide and proceed — it is the product source of truth, not an exhaustive spec.
11	- Never edit files under `docs/input/` — frozen product input, not project output.
12	- Never change the backend, its API contract, or its configuration — consume it as documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
13	- Never call an AI provider (Claude, Voyage AI) directly from the app — every AI feature, including semantic search, goes through the backend.
14	- Never commit `.env` or any credential — it is gitignored; it holds exactly `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
15	- Never write a visual value (color, font, spacing, radius) outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` — it is the single source, built from `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` section 3.
16	- Never implement an extension feature (`docs/input/requirements.md` section 2) — a menu entry may exist as a placeholder, nothing functional behind it.
17	- Implement functional requirements in the delivery order given in `docs/input/requirements.md` section 12, not request order.
18	
19	## Where things are
20	
21	- Product spec (requirements, acceptance criteria, screen flow, endpoint-to-requirement mapping, delivery order): `docs/input/requirements.md`
22	- Visual tokens and navigable states: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`; raw prototype: `docs/input/prototype/cerne-prototype.html`
23	- Backend API contract: `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`; path-to-function mapping: `docs/input/backend/README.md`; error taxonomy, sync-badge semantics, known bugs, test fixtures: rest of `docs/input/backend/`

29	## Conventions that differ from defaults
30	
31	- Call the backend only at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>`, never at the literal REST path shown in `openapi.yaml` — each operation's real URL is its `x-cerne-function` name, with path parameters appended as trailing segments. E.g. `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry` calls `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/chat-messages-retry/{id}/{userMessageId}` — the literal `/retry` segment does not exist in the real URL.
32	- Send header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>` on every call. Send `Authorization: Bearer <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>` only on the three operations with `security: []` in the contract (signup, login, refresh); send `Authorization: Bearer <user access token>` on every operation marked `bearerAuth`.
33	- Audio speech-to-text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml` — never send an audio file to the backend.
34	- Repositories return `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`); no repository signature outside this pattern (RNF09).
35	- Three layers per feature (`data/domain/presentation`) under `lib/features/<feature>/`; the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from `data/` (RNF06).
36	- RF10 (save chat message as entry) must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly — doing so also violates RNF06.

Implemented spec-1-1 in full. All four verification commands pass: `fvm flutter pub get` (no conflicts), `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` (generates `failure.freezed.dart`, no errors), `fvm flutter analyze` (zero issues), `fvm flutter test` (52/52 passing).

## What was done

**Scaffold**
- `fvm use 3.47.5` (already-cached stable patch) → `.fvmrc` + `.fvm/`.
- `fvm flutter create --platforms=ios --org com.cerne --project-name cerne .` → `pubspec.yaml`, `lib/main.dart`, `ios/`, `analysis_options.yaml`, `.metadata`, `test/` (removed the generated counter `widget_test.dart`).
- `pubspec.yaml`: added every Stack Pins package. Two pins from the architecture spine don't exist on pub.dev as written and I resolved them pragmatically: `freezed_annotation` pinned to `^3.1.0` (what `freezed ^4.0.3` actually requires — the spine's "freezed + freezed_annotation ^4.0.3" conflates the two packages' independent version lines) and `hive_ce_flutter` pinned to `^2.5.0` (its own version line; it in turn depends on `hive_ce ^2.22.0`, matching the spine). `json_annotation` added as the unlisted-but-required peer of `json_serializable`. Declared `.env` as a Flutter asset (gitignored, never committed) so `flutter_dotenv` can load it both at runtime and under `flutter test`.
- `.gitignore`: merged in standard Flutter/Dart/IDE/iOS ignores plus `*.freezed.dart`/`*.g.dart` (regenerated by build_runner, not committed) and `.fvm/flutter_sdk`, while preserving the existing `.env` entry.

**`lib/` — Structural Seed, verified to match exactly**
- `core/failure/failure.dart`: sealed `Failure` (freezed, new primary-constructor-era syntax) with all 14 subtypes, a `retryable` getter switch-derived from the 6 AD-4 codes (so `MalformedResponse` is hardcoded false by construction, not by parameter), and `Failure.fromCode(code, message)` mapping the 13 backend codes with an unrecognized-code fallback to `malformedResponse` (never throws).
- `core/network/url_builder.dart`, `header_interceptor.dart` (+ `access_token_provider.dart`, a small port/impl pair I added so the header rule has somewhere to read the current user token from before auth exists — backed by `flutter_secure_storage`), `retry_interceptor.dart` (500ms delay, max 2 retries, pure `errorCodeOf`/`shouldRetry` for testability), `api_client.dart` (the one façade mapping every dio outcome to `Either<Failure, T>`).
- `core/di/injection_container.dart` + `main.dart`: one `get_it` (`sl`), loads `.env`, registers `FlutterSecureStorage` → `AccessTokenProvider` → `UrlBuilder` → `Dio` (with both interceptors) → `ApiClient`.
- `core/resource.dart` (AD-12, implemented), `isolated_side_effect.dart` and `design_tokens.dart` (typed stubs only, per boundaries), `cache/` and `session/` (empty, `.gitkeep` only).
- `features/{auth,vault,entries,capture,chat,export,dashboard,account}/{data,domain,presentation}/.gitkeep` — no code.

**`test/`**
- `core/failure/failure_test.dart`: all 14 subtypes constructible, `fromCode` mapping for all 13 server codes + fallback, and an exact-set check that only the 6 AD-4 codes are retryable.
- `core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart`: pure-function coverage of `errorCodeOf`/`shouldRetry` across all 13 codes, plus an end-to-end mocked-`Dio` test proving a retryable error retries once and resolves, and a non-retryable error never calls `fetch`.
- `core/di/bootstrap_integration_test.dart`: resolves `Dio`/`FlutterSecureStorage`/`ApiClient` from the single `sl`, asserts the two custom interceptors are attached, and round-trips a real write/read through the DI-resolved `FlutterSecureStorage`. Caveat: no device/simulator/CI exists, so the native `plugins.it_nomads.com/flutter_secure_storage` method channel is faked with an in-memory map rather than exercising real Keychain — the DI wiring and the `FlutterSecureStorage` API surface are genuinely exercised, just not real native storage.
- `test/support/write_failure_matrix_helper.dart` (the reusable `runWriteFailureMatrix` helper, generic over any write call) + `write_failure_matrix_helper_test.dart` demonstrating it against `auth-signup` via a mocked `ApiClient` (no feature repository exists yet, per F000's boundaries, so the demo calls `ApiClient.post('auth-signup', ...)` directly — exactly the shape every later write-endpoint test will reuse).

**`AGENTS.md`**: replaced the "Running and verifying" TODO with the four real fvm-wrapped commands, the `.env`-as-asset note, and the no-device/CI caveat for the bootstrap test.

## Risks / left incomplete
- Nothing in-scope was skipped; no feature code, session logic, or design tokens were built (correctly out of scope per the boundaries).
- `AccessTokenProvider`/`SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` is a design decision I made (not explicitly spec'd) to give the header interceptor something to read a user token from before the auth feature exists — Story 1.3/1.4 should reuse it (`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken`) rather than inventing a second mechanism.
- `freezed_annotation`/`hive_ce_flutter` version pins deviate from the literal spine table for the reason above (those exact combinations don't resolve) — flagged inline in `pubspec.yaml` comments are not present, only in this report, so worth a human double-check against the spine if it's revised later.
- Nothing was committed to git — nine files are staged-ready but uncommitted (scaffold is all untracked/modified in `git status`), since committing wasn't requested.

Review of your Story 1.1 implementation (spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md) surfaced several patch-level findings — all trivially fixable, no spec renegotiation needed, no code reverted. 1. **lib/core/network/api_client.dart — `_mapDioException` can throw an uncaught TypeError.** `(data['message'] as String?)` throws if the backend ever sends a non-null, non-String `message` field (e.g. an int). This directly contradicts the method's own doc comment and RNF09 ("no dio/native exception ever escapes unmapped"). Fix: coerce safely, e.g. `data['message'] is String ? data['message'] as String : null`. Add a test case for a response body with a non-String `message` field, asserting it still returns `Left(Failure)` without throwing.

2. **lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart — `onRequest`'s actual header-decision logic has zero behavioral test.** The only existing test (`bootstrap_integration_test.dart`) just counts that one `HeaderInterceptor` is attached — it never calls `onRequest` or inspects the resulting headers. Add a dedicated unit test (e.g. `test/core/network/header_interceptor_test.dart`) that constructs `HeaderInterceptor` with a fake/mock `AccessTokenProvider`, calls `onRequest` against `RequestOptions` for (a) one of the 3 anon-only functions and (b) an arbitrary other function with a stored token and (c) with no stored token, then asserts `headers['apikey']` and `headers['Authorization']` directly in each case.

3. **lib/core/network/api_client.dart — `ApiClient`'s real send/mapping logic is never exercised under test.** The only test referencing `ApiClient` (`write_failure_matrix_helper_test.dart`) mocks the whole class away. Add a direct unit test for `ApiClient` using a mocked `Dio` (not a mocked `ApiClient`) covering: success response, a `DioException` with a `{code, message}` body (asserting correct `Failure` mapping), a `DioException` with no response at all (asserting `NetworkOffline`), and a non-`DioException` thrown by `Dio` (asserting `MalformedResponse`, not a crash).

4. **lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart — `onError`'s retry branch only catches `DioException` around the retried `_dio.fetch` call.** Any other exception type thrown there escapes unhandled and the request never resolves via `handler`. Broaden the catch to handle any exception from that retried fetch, falling back to `handler.next` (wrapped as needed) so the caller always gets a result.

5. **lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart — `onRequest` calls `_accessTokenProvider.readAccessToken()` with no guard.** A thrown `PlatformException` from the native secure-storage channel would propagate uncaught. Wrap that call in try/catch; on failure, proceed as if no token were found (omit `Authorization` rather than crash the request pipeline).

6. **lib/core/di/injection_container.dart — no `Dio` `BaseOptions` timeout configured.** A stalled connection can hang indefinitely instead of ever failing. Add sensible default timeouts (`connectTimeout`, `receiveTimeout`, `sendTimeout` — pick reasonable values, e.g. 10s connect / 30s receive, since no planning doc specifies exact numbers) when constructing `Dio()`. Add one line to the spec's `## Design Notes` section (non-frozen, so it's safe to append) documenting this as a 4th silent-gap decision, same pattern as the existing retry-policy note.

7. **test/core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart — the end-to-end `onError` group never covers the retry-exhausted path.** Only "retries once and succeeds" and "never retries" are covered. 8. **lib/core/network/url_builder.dart — `build()` doesn't URL-encode its segments**, and has no dedicated unit test despite its own doc comment calling it "independently testable." Fix: `Uri.encodeComponent` each segment before joining. Add `test/core/network/url_builder_test.dart` covering normal segments, a segment needing encoding, and the trailing-slash-stripping behavior on `baseUrl`. Also add a small test for `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf` (can live in the same new header_interceptor_test.dart from item 2) covering a bare function path and a path with trailing path params.

input.message:
Applied all 11 patch-round findings to the Story 1.1 codebase. Re-ran the spec's verification commands after: `fvm flutter pub get` (no conflicts), `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` (clean, no errors), `fvm flutter analyze` (zero issues), `fvm flutter test` (70/70 passing, up from 52 before this round). Nothing was reverted; the "ios orientation lock" item was left alone per your note.

Per-item changes:

1. **`lib/core/network/api_client.dart` — unsafe `message` cast.** `_mapDioException` now does `final message = data['message']; ... (message is String ? message : null) ?? e.message ?? 'Unknown error'` instead of `data['message'] as String?`. Added a test case in the new `api_client_test.dart` with an int `message` field, asserting `Left(Validation)` with no throw.

2. **`test/core/network/header_interceptor_test.dart` (new).** Constructs `HeaderInterceptor` with a mocked `AccessTokenProvider`, calls `onRequest` directly, and asserts headers for: an anon-only function (`auth-login` → apikey + anon bearer, `readAccessToken` never called), another function with a stored token (apikey + user bearer), another function with no stored token (apikey only, no `Authorization` key at all), plus (doubling as item 5's regression test) a thrown exception from `readAccessToken` (apikey only, no crash). Also covers `functionNameOf` for a bare path, a path with trailing params, and a relative path (item 8's header-interceptor ask).

3. **`test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` (new).** Mocks `Dio` directly (not `ApiClient`) and exercises `_send`/`_mapDioException` for real: success → `Right`, `DioException` with `{code, message}` body → correctly-typed `Failure` (`RateLimited`), non-String `message` → still `Left` (item 1's regression), `DioException` with no response → `Left(NetworkOffline)`, a non-`DioException` thrown by `Dio` → `Left(MalformedResponse)`, and a null response body → `Left(MalformedResponse)`.

4. **`lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart` — narrow catch on the retried fetch.** Added a second `catch (retryError)` (any type) alongside the existing `on DioException`, wrapping the caught value into a synthetic `DioException` and routing it through `handler.next` so any exception type from the retried `_dio.fetch` still reaches the caller instead of escaping.

5. **`lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart` — unguarded `readAccessToken()`.** Wrapped the call in try/catch; on any thrown exception, proceeds with `userToken = null` (omits `Authorization`) instead of propagating. Covered by the new header_interceptor_test.dart case above.

6. **`lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` — no `Dio` timeouts.** `Dio()` is now constructed with `BaseOptions(connectTimeout: 10s, receiveTimeout: 30s, sendTimeout: 30s)`. Added a 4th Design Notes bullet to the spec file documenting this as a silent-gap decision (same pattern as the existing retry-policy note).

7. **`test/core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart` — added retry-exhausted end-to-end case.** New test feeds the thrown/retried `DioException` back into `onError` round-by-round (simulating the real Dio pipeline re-entering `onError`, since a bare mock doesn't loop by itself) through `maxRetries`, then asserts `handler.resolve` was never called, `handler.next` was finally called with an error carrying `attempt == maxRetries`, and `Dio.fetch` was called exactly `maxRetries` times (not a 3rd time).

8. **`lib/core/network/url_builder.dart` — no URL-encoding.** `build()` now runs every segment through `Uri.encodeComponent` before joining. Added `test/core/network/url_builder_test.dart` (new) covering plain segments, path-param ordering, trailing-slash stripping on `baseUrl`, and a segment needing encoding (spaces + a literal `/`). The `functionNameOf` tests landed in header_interceptor_test.dart per your suggested grouping (item 2 above).

9. **`.env.example` (new)** at the repo root with `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL=` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=` placeholders, no real values. AGENTS.md's "Running and verifying" section now says to copy it to `.env`.

10. **Spec Design Notes — version-pin resolution recorded.** Added a bullet to `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-...md`'s (non-frozen) `## Design Notes` section explaining why `freezed_annotation` is pinned `^3.1.0` (what `freezed ^4.0.3` actually requires) and `hive_ce_flutter` is pinned `^2.5.0` (its own independent version line, itself depending on `hive_ce ^2.22.0`), so the resolution survives outside chat history. No code change.

11. **AGENTS.md wording fix.** "`Failure`'s `freezed`/`json_serializable` output" → "`Failure`'s `freezed` output today, plus `json_serializable` output for any later feature's DTOs."

Files touched this round: `lib/core/network/api_client.dart`, `header_interceptor.dart`, `retry_interceptor.dart`, `url_builder.dart`; `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart`; `test/core/network/{header_interceptor_test.dart, api_client_test.dart, url_builder_test.dart}` (new) and `retry_interceptor_test.dart` (extended); `.env.example` (new); `AGENTS.md`; `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md`.

Nothing left incomplete from this list. Still uncommitted (as before) — no commit was made since none was requested.
